summary: Encrypted SAML NameID decryption mismatch causes 403s for SSO users in private deployment
description: MedLex reports that after they enabled encrypted SAML assertions on their IdP, users can complete the SSO redirect flow but receive 403 Forbidden when calling the Redwood private API. A subset of users (all SSO-authenticated users) are unable to map roles and therefore cannot access the private deployment. No 5xx from the serving runtime; failures are authorization-level (403).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private deployment with customer SAML IdP metadata (IdP sends EncryptedAssertions).
2) Perform SP-initiated SSO login using SAML with encrypted NameID/assertion enabled on IdP side.
3) Observe redirect back to identity-proxy -> session established -> attempt to call Redwood API -> 403 returned.
4) Check identity-proxy logs for decryption/signature verification messages and RBAC mapping traces.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z identity-proxy[auth] WARN failed to decrypt EncryptedAssertion: keyName mismatch (expected key alias 'medlex-sp-enc', got none)
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z identity-proxy[auth] INFO SAML Response validated (signature ok) but Subject/NameID extraction failed
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z access-checker ERROR no principal email extracted -> role mapping failed -> returning 403
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: signature/JWKS rotation issue. Logs show signature validation succeeded but decryption failed.
IdP is sending EncryptedAssertion elements with KeyInfo/KeyName that did not match the customer's uploaded decryption certificate alias in our onboarding bundle.
Private identity-proxy version 1.12.2 requires KeyInfo.KeyName to map to a keystore alias; if KeyName is missing or mismatched the assertion remains encrypted and NameID cannot be extracted.
Customer confirmed they recently enabled 'encrypt assertions' in Okta and uploaded a new public key but left KeyName blank (Okta default).
Reproduced on a staging private cluster by toggling encrypted assertions and removing KeyName from metadata.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:03 - Support (Ava): Hi MedLex — thanks for the report. Can you confirm whether your IdP is sending EncryptedAssertion elements and whether the SAML metadata includes a KeyName?

2026-03-10 15:20 - Customer (Sarah L., MedLex IdP Admin): We turned on Encrypt Assertions for PII. We uploaded a public encryption cert via the Okta UI but did not set a KeyName. We see the login redirect succeed but then 403s.

2026-03-10 16:40 - Support (Diego): We reproduced the failure in a staging private environment. identity-proxy was unable to map the decryption KeyInfo because KeyName was absent; NameID remained encrypted and role mapping failed.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Eng (Diego): Deployed hotfix in identity-proxy (PR #487) to fallback to matching KeyInfo.X509Certificate when KeyName is missing. Also added a clear debug log when encrypted assertion cannot be matched.
2026-03-11 12:20 - Customer (Sarah): After the hotfix was deployed to the private tenant and we re-ran a test, SSO users can access the API. Thank you.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Ava): Closing ticket; created follow-up to update onboarding docs.
resolution: Hotfix deployed to identity-proxy to support certificate-only matching for encrypted assertions; customer re-tested and confirmed access restored.
resolution_notes: Applied identity-proxy patch: fallback to X509Certificate match if KeyName missing (merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/487).
Rolled patch to MedLex private cluster (us-west) as a targeted config update during low-traffic window (2026-03-11 02:00 UTC).
Customer onboarded to recommended checklist: either include KeyName in IdP encryption KeyInfo or ensure decryption cert is present and matches X509Certificate in metadata.
Added diagnostic log lines to aid future debugging: logs now include which KeyInfo match path was attempted (KeyName vs X509Certificate).
Follow-up action: update Confluence onboarding page and add a new test case to private deploy e2e for EncryptedAssertion without KeyName. (Action owner: Diego Martinez, due 2026-03-19).
